areas.finding: Ordinary brown Atlas moose retains broad drooping muzzle, small hanging throat bell, high shaggy shoulders, long legs and broad palmate antlers; no armored companion or branching elk-antler substitute.
All four cardinals and front/rear obliques are distinct, labeled and complete with antler tips, ears, tail and hooves uncropped.

Six native antler closeups confirm one bilateral pair of broad flat palms with coherent main upward tines and forward brow projections. Opposing views preserve the palm masses; minor tine overlaps vary naturally with perspective, without a concrete missing branch or extra antler base.
Four long legs with cloven dark hoof forms resolve through profiles and obliques, with grounded feet and consistent fore/hind joint direction.
Paired ears, long drooping muzzle and one small throat bell stay attached in the visible front/profile/oblique views.
One short tail remains at the rump; shaggy high shoulders and brown torso masses agree across front, rear and side rotations.
Grouped sculpted fur, warm antler material, expressive face and clear studio grounding meet the Havenline static-reference style.

source_interpretation_limit: The Atlas supplies one small source pose. Reverse fur and fine tine surfaces are authored reference interpretation; this static review does not establish native antler topology, rigging or movement.
minor_polish_limit: Fine fur tufts and tine thickness vary illustratively. The two palmate structures and principal attachments remain coherent across every inspected angle.
